title: Attempt run status
description: The status.json at the root of every sealed evidence bundle: what benchctl attempted, how far it got, and how each subject exited. Written on every path including crash, timeout, and interrupt by the always-seal supervisor in crates/benchctl/src/seal.rs. Documentation mirror of the RunStatus serde type in crates/bench-schema/src/status.rs, which is the source of truth and pins the snake_case wire strings below. Optional fields are OMITTED rather than serialized as null: the type marks them `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"`, so a reader tells 'absent' from 'present and null' by the key not being there at all.

experiment_id.description: 64-character lowercase hex identity of the resolved intent. Absent when the attempt failed before resolution produced an id, which is exactly the case the always-seal rule exists for.

execution_status.description: Worst-wins precedence: timed_out beats crashed beats partial beats complete. A complete run can still be invalid; validity is the separate kafkars.classification.v1 axis.

failure_reason.description: Why the status is not complete, in one line. Absent for a complete run.

interrupted.description: True when SIGINT or SIGTERM reached benchctl; an interrupted run seals as partial.

subjects.description: One entry per subject, in execution order. A failing subject records evidence and the run continues; there is no fail-fast.

execution.description: Process exit facts. Absent when the subject was never spawned, for example after an earlier phase failed.

exit_code.description: Exit status when the process exited normally. Absent when it died on a signal, and absent together with signal when it was never spawned.

signal.description: Terminating signal number when the child died from a signal. Mutually exclusive with exit_code on Unix.

adapter_outcome.description: outcome field of this subject's kafkars.adapter-status.v1 document. Absent when the adapter wrote no status, which is what a crashed subject looks like.

result_present.description: Whether a parseable result.json was found for this subject.

verification.description: Read-back verification of this subject's measured and warmup topics. Always present; an empty object means neither topic was verified.

phases.description: Phase records of the attempt state machine, in the order they were attempted. A skipped phase makes the run partial.

name.description: Phase name from the control plane's state machine, for example seal-inputs, topic-create, or subject:<name>:run.

outcome.description: Whether the phase ran and did what it was supposed to. skipped is a deferred phase, not a pass.

detail.description: One line of detail, when there is something worth saying. Absent otherwise.

verificationOutcome.description: What the configured verifier tool did for one topic.

ran.description: Whether the tool ran at all. False means the check was skipped, which is a deferred check rather than a pass.

valid.description: The tool's verdict, when it produced one. Absent when it did not.

exit_code.description: The tool's exit status, when it exited normally. Absent when it did not.
